facts.text: Cedarville sits in southern Prince George's County, bordered by Brandywine, Croom, Baden, and Charles County.
The area was a long‑time homeland of the Piscataway people, who used its milder climate for winter camping and game hunting.
In 1680 the Piscataway built Zekiah Fort near Cedarville to defend against northern tribes, a fort that stood until about 1695.
The Maryland Department of Natural Resources bought 2,631 acres in 1930 to create Cedarville State Forest, a demonstration area for sustainable forestry.
The Civilian Conservation Corps operated Camp S‑54 at Cedarville from 1933 to 1941, planting thousands of loblolly pines with 192 African‑American enrollees.
In 2023 a lease expiration sparked protests over a former Nike missile base lease, leading to a halt of eviction and plans to donate the land to the Piscataway tribe.
